title: Wowza vs Ant Media Server: Which Fits Your Team in 2026?
description: Wowza prices its streaming server by instance and publishes no amounts; Ant Media lists $129 per instance monthly and a $0.35 hourly Flex rate. Compare licensing.
intro: Wowza Streaming Engine and Ant Media Server are both streaming servers you can run on your own infrastructure, so the licensing terms matter as much as the feature list. Wowza says its cost is based on the number of server instances you deploy but shows no price amounts on the pages opened. Ant Media publishes monthly, annual and hourly figures. This page compares the two on deployment options, pricing transparency and trial terms, using each vendor's own pages.
verdict: Choose Ant Media Server if you want to budget from a published price list, with a 14-day Enterprise trial and a pay-by-the-hour option. Choose Wowza if you need the widest deployment menu, including air-gapped installs, and are comfortable asking for a quote and premium support terms. Either way, count instances first, because both meters follow them.
pick_a: Pick Wowza if you run on-premises, edge or air-gapped environments, want a managed OVP option beside the server, and accept a sales conversation for pricing.
pick_b: Pick Ant Media Server if WebRTC latency is the draw, you want prices you can put in a spreadsheet today, and per-instance monthly or hourly billing suits your load.

text: Wowza describes Streaming Engine as video streaming server software for live and on-demand video. Its pricing page explains that the cost is based on the number of server instances you deploy, and offers a trial and premium support plans. No amounts are printed in the text read, so a budget starts with a conversation or the trial.

Ant Media Server is described as a real-time streaming engine supporting WebRTC, CMAF, HLS, RTMP, RTSP, SRT and more. Its pricing page prints numbers: Flex at $0.35 per instance-hour, a monthly plan with a regular price of $129 per instance per month and an annual regular price of $1,308 per year. The price tags also reference a Black Friday deal link, which suggests the regular prices are the ones to model.

Since both vendors meter per server instance, the arithmetic starts with how many instances your peak load needs. At Ant Media's listed rates, one instance for a month costs $129, while the annual option works out to $109 per month on $1,308. Flex at $0.35 per hour equals $252 for a 720-hour month if run continuously, so it only wins when instances are switched off for much of the month.

For Wowza the same exercise needs a quote, so the comparison is incomplete until you have one. Ask for a price per instance and per support tier in writing, and ask whether the trial converts to a paid license without reinstalling.

Wowza lists on-premises, cloud, hybrid, edge and air-gapped deployments for Streaming Engine, and it sells Flowplayer OVP as a fully managed cloud streaming platform for teams that would rather not run servers at all. That spread is the strongest case for Wowza in locked-down networks.

Ant Media says you can deploy on your own infrastructure or any cloud, and its pricing page mentions cloud marketplaces and self-hosted plans. Its site lists SDKs for iOS, Android, Unity, React Native, Flutter and JavaScript, which helps game and app teams that need to publish from inside their own client.

Both let you test before paying. Wowza offers a Start a Trial option, and Ant Media offers a 14-day free trial on the Enterprise Edition. Fourteen days is short for a load test, so plan the test in advance and prepare your encoder inputs before starting the clock.

Ant Media also mentions an own-license option for long-term projects. If a fixed license appeals to your finance team more than recurring instance fees, ask about its terms. Wowza's pages read do not describe a comparable option.

For a [streaming media server](/software/best-streaming-media-servers) shortlist, the choice often reduces to latency and procurement. Ant Media's homepage claims about 300 ms latency and a 99.99% uptime SLA; both are vendor claims and worth verifying in your own test. Wowza's pitch leans on deployment range and a managed path through Flowplayer OVP.

If you are building an esports watch party or an interactive auction, test WebRTC behavior first. If you are streaming an internal broadcast inside a closed network, the air-gapped option on Wowza's list may settle the matter.

faqs.q: How much does Wowza Streaming Engine cost?
faqs.a: The pages opened do not show amounts. Wowza says the cost is based on the number of server instances you deploy and lists a trial plus premium support plans, so a price needs a quote or demo request.

faqs.q: What does Ant Media Server cost?
faqs.a: The pricing page lists Flex at $0.35 per instance-hour, a monthly plan at a regular $129 per instance per month and an annual regular price of $1,308 per year. It also offers an own-license option for long-term projects.

faqs.q: Is there a free trial for each?
faqs.a: Yes. Wowza offers a Start a Trial option on its pricing page, and Ant Media offers a 14-day free trial on its Enterprise Edition. Check the length and conversion terms for Wowza before testing.

Wowza lists air-gapped deployment among its Streaming Engine options. Ant Media's pages say it runs on your own infrastructure, which could include isolated networks, but air-gapped use is not named there.

faqs.q: Does either offer a managed cloud service?
faqs.a: Wowza does, through Flowplayer OVP, which it describes as a fully managed, cloud-based streaming platform. Ant Media's pricing mentions cloud marketplaces, but a managed service is not described on the pages read.

sources.fact: Wowza describes its Streaming Engine as video streaming server software for live and on-demand video, deployable on-prem, in the cloud, at the edge or air-gapped.
Wowza's product list includes Flowplayer OVP, a fully managed, cloud-based streaming platform for live and on-demand video.
The Wowza pricing page says server cost is based on the number of instances deployed, offers a trial and lists premium support plans.
Ant Media Server is a real-time streaming engine supporting WebRTC, CMAF, HLS, RTMP, RTSP, SRT and more, deployed on your own infrastructure or any cloud.

The Ant Media pricing page lists Flex at $0.35 per instance-hour, a monthly plan with a regular price of $129 per instance per month, an annual regular price of $1,308 and a 14-day free trial on Enterprise Edition.
